originalText:
Over the years we have spent quite a lot of time thinking about the question: “What makes a good investment?” We often get the following type of responses when we pose this question to others:

“We believe it is successful if it pays a good dividend,” or “We believe it is successful if it goes up in price.”

We counter with:

“Well, suppose it is a private company, and there is no share price discovery.”

Or, alternatively, we say:

“Suppose that the business (investment) is confronted with so many good reinvestment opportunities that they pay no dividend.”

What are we left with in trying to answer this question?

We have concluded that the only real way to measure the success of an investment is by identifying the real growth in economic value per unit of ownership.

We speak in terms of “per unit of ownership” because aggregate growth in economic value can completely elude the individual holder if accompanied by commensurate growth in the units of ownership, leaving the individual owner without any individual growth in value.

In the public markets, where we spend the majority of our time and attention, we examine the balance sheets of interesting businesses to see if we can make general evaluations of the growth in this real economic value per share. Sometimes it is quite easily measured by the growth in book value per share. Other times this easy approach is altogether without value due to the oddities of accounting rules.

Therefore, we look to investment in two businesses that lend themselves well to the importance of growth in book value per share, and prominently display that information in their published financial reports. In our view, growth in book value per share is tantamount to a business’ actual real economic earnings and it allows us to establish our valuation calculations based on this per share growth in book value. We examine what the historical growth in book value per share has been and make an estimate of what we think growth is likely to be over the next five to ten years, on average. We assign an estimate to the forward year and relate it to the current share price, giving us a multiple which is often very different from the normal Wall Street earnings estimate multiples.

Our calculation frequently suggests the business is much cheaper than conventional methodologies indicate. We believe this gives us an edge.

In many other businesses that we own, book value per share calculations are largely distorted by share buybacks and other accounting applications. For a strong business, book value typically understates economic value. Warren Buffett famously wrote a piece many years ago identifying what he called “economic goodwill,” an item which has no tangible value (and no precise relationship to accounting goodwill), but nonetheless creates earnings. Accounting gives us some guideposts for gauging real economic value, but we are left to figure out the details using our own interpretation of what is actually occurring in the business.

Clearly, there are many considerations we make along the way, like the quality and sustainability of the business, the skill and quality of the people, and the availability of reinvestment opportunities.

When all is said and done, no matter how we arrive at the calculation of the future growth in real economic value per share, we ask, “What is the best value and opportunity today?” It all comes down to rate of return.

When an individual is confronted with investment opportunities across many different asset classes – for example, art, real estate, precious metals, private businesses, or public securities – the only way in which to make comparisons (apart from the different characteristics of said investments – you can hang a picture on your wall or hang a piece of jewelry around your neck) is rate of return. It is the only standard by which all can be measured!

Further, when thinking about investing in bank CDs, there are often small differences in the rates being paid and the method of compounding used in the calculation, even as all the choices are guaranteed by the U.S. government. So, again, it comes down to rate of return.

In summary, our constant goal, regardless of the opportunity type, is to establish a reasonable expectation of an investment’s rate of growth in real economic value per share coincident with actual experience, and evaluate each and every opportunity by this standard: the bottom line of all investing is rate of return.

Chuck Akre

The investment examples included herein have been selected based on objective, non-performance selection criteria, solely to provide general examples of the research and investment processes of Akre Capital Management. The investment examples should not be construed as an indicator of future performance. The information presented above should not be considered a recommendation to purchase or sell any particular security. There can be no assurance that any securities discussed herein will be a part of any portfolio or, if sold, will not be repurchased.

segments.zh: 多年来，我们花了相当多的时间思考这样一个问题：“什么样的投资才是好投资？”当我们向别人提出这个问题时，常常得到下面这类回答：

segments.original: “We believe it is successful if it pays a good dividend,” or “We believe it is successful if it goes up in price.”
segments.en: “We believe it is successful if it pays a good dividend,” or “We believe it is successful if it goes up in price.”
segments.zh: “我们认为，只要分红丰厚，就是成功的投资。”或者，“我们认为，只要价格上涨，就是成功的投资。”

segments.original: We counter with:
segments.en: We counter with:
segments.zh: 我们会反问：

segments.original: “Well, suppose it is a private company, and there is no share price discovery.”
segments.en: “Well, suppose it is a private company, and there is no share price discovery.”
segments.zh: “那么，假设这是一家非上市公司，并不存在股票价格发现机制呢？”

segments.original: Or, alternatively, we say:
segments.en: Or, alternatively, we say:
segments.zh: 或者，我们会说：

segments.original: “Suppose that the business (investment) is confronted with so many good reinvestment opportunities that they pay no dividend.”
segments.en: “Suppose that the business (investment) is confronted with so many good reinvestment opportunities that they pay no dividend.”
segments.zh: “假设这家企业（这项投资）面前有如此多的优质再投资机会，以至于它根本不分红呢？”

segments.original: What are we left with in trying to answer this question?
segments.en: What are we left with in trying to answer this question?
segments.zh: 那么，在回答这个问题时，我们还剩下什么衡量依据？

segments.original: We have concluded that the only real way to measure the success of an investment is by identifying the real growth in economic value per unit of ownership.
segments.en: We have concluded that the only real way to measure the success of an investment is by identifying the real growth in economic value per unit of ownership.
segments.zh: 我们的结论是：衡量一项投资是否成功，唯一真正有效的方法，就是确定每单位所有权所对应的经济价值的实际增长。

segments.original: We speak in terms of “per unit of ownership” because aggregate growth in economic value can completely elude the individual holder if accompanied by commensurate growth in the units of ownership, leaving the individual owner without any individual growth in value.
segments.en: We speak in terms of “per unit of ownership” because aggregate growth in economic value can completely elude the individual holder if accompanied by commensurate growth in the units of ownership, leaving the individual owner without any individual growth in value.
segments.zh: 我们之所以使用“每单位所有权”这个说法，是因为，如果经济价值总量的增长伴随着所有权单位数量的同比例增加，那么个别持有人完全可能分享不到这种增长，其个人持有部分的价值也就没有任何增长。

segments.original: In the public markets, where we spend the majority of our time and attention, we examine the balance sheets of interesting businesses to see if we can make general evaluations of the growth in this real economic value per share. segments.en: In the public markets, where we spend the majority of our time and attention, we examine the balance sheets of interesting businesses to see if we can make general evaluations of the growth in this real economic value per share. Sometimes it is quite easily measured by the growth in book value per share. Other times this easy approach is altogether without value due to the oddities of accounting rules.
segments.zh: 在公开市场上，我们投入了绝大多数时间和精力。我们会审视那些值得关注的企业的资产负债表，看看能否对这种每股实际经济价值的增长作出大致评估。有时，这可以很容易地通过每股账面价值的增长来衡量。另一些时候，由于会计规则的特殊之处，这种简便方法却毫无价值。

In our view, growth in book value per share is tantamount to a business’ actual real economic earnings and it allows us to establish our valuation calculations based on this per share growth in book value. We examine what the historical growth in book value per share has been and make an estimate of what we think growth is likely to be over the next five to ten years, on average. We assign an estimate to the forward year and relate it to the current share price, giving us a multiple which is often very different from the normal Wall Street earnings estimate multiples.
segments.zh: 因此，我们考察了对两家企业的投资：对于这两家企业而言，每股账面价值增长的重要性十分适用，而且它们都在已公布的财务报告中醒目地披露了这项信息。在我们看来，每股账面价值的增长相当于一家企业真正的实际经济收益，因此我们可以以每股账面价值的增长为基础进行估值计算。我们考察每股账面价值过去的增长情况，并估计未来五到十年平均可能实现怎样的增长。我们对未来一年的数值作出估算，再将其与当前股价相联系，得出一个估值倍数；这个倍数往往与华尔街通常依据盈利预测所计算的倍数大不相同。

segments.original: Our calculation frequently suggests the business is much cheaper than conventional methodologies indicate. We believe this gives us an edge.
segments.en: Our calculation frequently suggests the business is much cheaper than conventional methodologies indicate. We believe this gives us an edge.
segments.zh: 我们的计算常常表明，企业的价格比传统方法所显示的便宜得多。我们相信，这让我们具有优势。

Warren Buffett famously wrote a piece many years ago identifying what he called “economic goodwill,” an item which has no tangible value (and no precise relationship to accounting goodwill), but nonetheless creates earnings. Accounting gives us some guideposts for gauging real economic value, but we are left to figure out the details using our own interpretation of what is actually occurring in the business.
segments.en: In many other businesses that we own, book value per share calculations are largely distorted by share buybacks and other accounting applications. For a strong business, book value typically understates economic value. Warren Buffett famously wrote a piece many years ago identifying what he called “economic goodwill,” an item which has no tangible value (and no precise relationship to accounting goodwill), but nonetheless creates earnings. Accounting gives us some guideposts for gauging real economic value, but we are left to figure out the details using our own interpretation of what is actually occurring in the business.
segments.zh: 在我们持有的许多其他企业中，股票回购及其他会计处理使每股账面价值的计算结果受到很大扭曲。对于一家实力雄厚的企业，账面价值通常会低估经济价值。许多年前，沃伦·巴菲特写过一篇著名的文章，阐明了他所说的“经济商誉”：这是一种没有有形价值、却仍能创造收益的东西，而且它与会计商誉之间也没有精确的对应关系。会计为我们衡量实际经济价值提供了一些路标，但具体细节仍需我们根据自己对企业实际经营状况的理解来弄清楚。

segments.original: Clearly, there are many considerations we make along the way, like the quality and sustainability of the business, the skill and quality of the people, and the availability of reinvestment opportunities.
segments.en: Clearly, there are many considerations we make along the way, like the quality and sustainability of the business, the skill and quality of the people, and the availability of reinvestment opportunities.
segments.zh: 显然，在这个过程中，我们会考虑许多因素，例如企业的质量和可持续性、人员的能力和素质，以及再投资机会是否充足。

segments.original: When all is said and done, no matter how we arrive at the calculation of the future growth in real economic value per share, we ask, “What is the best value and opportunity today?” It all comes down to rate of return.
segments.en: When all is said and done, no matter how we arrive at the calculation of the future growth in real economic value per share, we ask, “What is the best value and opportunity today?” It all comes down to rate of return.
segments.zh: 归根结底，无论我们如何计算每股实际经济价值的未来增长，我们都会问：“今天，哪里最有价值，哪里有最好的机会？”这一切最终都取决于回报率。

segments.original: When an individual is confronted with investment opportunities across many different asset classes – for example, art, real estate, precious metals, private businesses, or public securities – the only way in which to make comparisons (apart from the different characteristics of said investments – you can hang a picture on your wall or hang a piece of jewelry around your neck) is rate of return. It is the only standard by which all can be measured!
segments.en: When an individual is confronted with investment opportunities across many different asset classes – for example, art, real estate, precious metals, private businesses, or public securities – the only way in which to make comparisons (apart from the different characteristics of said investments – you can hang a picture on your wall or hang a piece of jewelry around your neck) is rate of return. It is the only standard by which all can be measured!
segments.zh: 当一个人面对许多不同资产类别的投资机会时，例如艺术品、房地产、贵金属、非上市企业或公开交易证券，除了这些投资各自的不同特征之外——你可以把一幅画挂在墙上，也可以把一件珠宝戴在脖子上——唯一可以用来进行比较的，就是回报率。它是能够衡量所有这些投资的唯一标准！

segments.original: Further, when thinking about investing in bank CDs, there are often small differences in the rates being paid and the method of compounding used in the calculation, even as all the choices are guaranteed by the U.S. government. So, again, it comes down to rate of return.
segments.en: Further, when thinking about investing in bank CDs, there are often small differences in the rates being paid and the method of compounding used in the calculation, even as all the choices are guaranteed by the U.S. government. So, again, it comes down to rate of return.
segments.zh: 此外，在考虑投资银行定期存单时，即便所有选项都由美国政府提供担保，它们支付的利率以及计算时采用的复利方式也往往存在细微差异。因此，归根结底，仍然是回报率。

segments.original: In summary, our constant goal, regardless of the opportunity type, is to establish a reasonable expectation of an investment’s rate of growth in real economic value per share coincident with actual experience, and evaluate each and every opportunity by this standard: the bottom line of all investing is rate of return.
segments.en: In summary, our constant goal, regardless of the opportunity type, is to establish a reasonable expectation of an investment’s rate of growth in real economic value per share coincident with actual experience, and evaluate each and every opportunity by this standard: the bottom line of all investing is rate of return.
segments.zh: 总之，无论机会属于哪一种类型，我们始终不变的目标，都是对一项投资的每股实际经济价值增长率形成与实际经验相符的合理预期，并以这一标准评估每一个机会：所有投资归根结底都是回报率。
